title: Tesla confirms Autopilot/FSD was ‘engaged’ when car crossed a median and killed a man
key_facts: On Saturday 22 Aug 2026 a Tesla crossed the grass median of Route 55 in Vineland, New Jersey, hit a tree and struck an SUV head-on.
The SUV driver, Phillip Eastman, 68, of Springfield, Pennsylvania, was killed; the Tesla driver and an SUV passenger were taken to hospital with moderate injuries.
Police described it as a driver who lost control; no early report mentioned driver assistance.
Tesla's report to NHTSA, made under a Standing General Order, lists the driver-assist 'Engagement Status' as 'Verified Engaged' for a 2021 Model Y.
Tesla redacted the crash narrative, software version and whether the road was in the system's approved area.
Electrek says 'engaged within 30 seconds of impact' is the reporting trigger, not proof the system was steering; the driver may have been overriding it.
Eastman had just been sworn in as a Springfield School District board member and coached youth and high-school ice hockey for nearly three decades.
quote_evidence: Under a NHTSA Standing General Order, automakers must report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed.
“Engaged within 30 seconds of impact” is the reporting trigger, not proof the system was steering when the car crossed the median.
Then it redacts the fields that would explain what the car did: the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows what Tesla's filing does and does not establish about driver assistance in a fatal crash.
notes: Electrek investigation matching crashes to redacted NHTSA data. The pool headline ("confirms engaged when car ... killed a man") overstates what the filing proves, so score lowered by 1 and headline worded cautiously.
